name: ow_nav_w0
doc: Stands in for saves/ow_w0.state, the original interactive 1000 A.D. overworld capture (ct.exe --navworld from its checkpoint saves/ow_w0.state.chk): the pad --navworld played from that checkpoint, recorded with CT_ORACLE_PADLOG -- its lead-slot probe, Mom's talk and Lucca's naming screen (A, Start), the 200 G allowance, out of the front door -- then the overworld settles. Under the rule the world load ends 4 frames sooner than on the plain oracle that made the capture, so the settle is 236 frames where --navworld ran 240: the ambient object blocks $0B30-$1B30 (the house's leftovers in the dead blocks included) then equal the capture byte for byte. The rest of the WRAM differs in 35 bytes, values 2-3 apart ($4B, a $0500 table at stride 12, two 5-byte runs of digit tiles at $2C2F/$2F68; not traced, likely the 4 frames the rule takes off the world load) and stack garbage ($06CF-$06FB); pack_world reads none of them.
